transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Um... well. Occupational health sent me. They, um... they said my weight is too low. Dangerously low, they called it. For someone running presses and doing fabrication all day. I just... I thought I was just getting leaner. More disciplined, you know? But they made me come here.
Have you been worried about gaining weight or feeling like you might be too thin, even if others might not see it that way?

I don't think I'm too thin. But... yeah, I guess I do worry about gaining. 

It's just... if the scale goes up, even a little bit, I... I don't know, I kind of panic. I just feel like I'm going to lose all the control I've worked for. I just really don't want to end up heavy again.
Have you been doing anything, like limiting how much you eat, making yourself sick, or exercising a lot more than usual, to keep your weight down?

I don't make myself sick. I just... keep things strict, I guess. 

Mostly it's just coffee before the early shift. Um... maybe half a protein bar at lunch. And then just a small bowl of vegetables later, after yoga. 

I just... if I eat more than that, it makes the whole day feel out of control. So I stick to that.
Do you feel like certain parts of your body are too large, or do you look in the mirror and feel like you're bigger than you actually are?

Um... yeah, I guess. 

I mean... when I catch my reflection in the shop window, or... or the bathroom mirror at work... I just... all I can really focus on is my stomach. And my thighs. They just still look... too big. 

And... I don't know, if I notice it, it just kind of ruins how I feel about myself for the rest of the day.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like missing periods or them stopping altogether?
Um... no. I haven't really noticed anything like that. They just seem normal, I guess. I don't really keep close track.
How much does your concern about your weight or body shape interfere with your daily life, like at work or when you're with friends and family?

Um... I guess it affects work mostly. 

The... occupational health rep at the plant flagged my weight recently. So... they pulled me off some of the press work. And they keep pressuring me to go to urgent care, which is... it's just disrupting my shifts. 

I'm missing hours, so... it's getting harder to keep up with the bills at home. But... yeah, that's really it.
Have you gone more than three months without having a period, or have you noticed that your periods have become very infrequent?
Um... no. Like I said... I haven't missed any. It's just... normal.
Can you tell me about the lowest weight you’ve reached recently, and how you felt about it at the time?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't... I don't weigh myself that often. I just... I feel fine about how I am right now. It's... it's not really a big deal.
Can you describe how you feel or what you do when you think about gaining even a small amount of weight?

Um... I don't know. I just... I really don't want to gain anything. 

If the scale goes up, even just a little bit, I... I start to panic. It feels like... like I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for. And... I just can't end up heavy again. I can't.
Do you find yourself thinking about food, weight, or body shape even when you're not eating or planning meals—like during work or when you're trying to relax?

Um... I don't know. Not really, I guess. 

When I'm at work... I just focus on my job. I'm pretty busy at the shop, so I don't really... sit around dwelling on things like that. I just try to keep my mind on what I'm doing.
Do you judge yourself mainly based on how much you weigh or how your body looks?

Um... I guess so. Yeah. 

It's just... if I catch my reflection, like in the shop window at work or... or the bathroom mirror... I just see my stomach. And my thighs. They just... they look too big. And if I see that, it just... it kind of ruins my whole day. I can't really feel good about anything else after that.
Have you intentionally lost weight or tried to keep your weight as low as possible because you were afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat?

Um... I mean, I try to keep it down, yeah. 

I just... I watch what I eat. I don't really want to get big. So I just... try to be careful. That's all.
Do you find that your weight or how your body looks affects how you see yourself overall—like whether you feel good about yourself or not?

Um... I mean, like I was just saying... yeah. 

If I catch sight of myself in the bathroom mirror and my stomach looks big... it just ruins how I feel about myself. For the whole day, really. I just... I don't feel good if I look like that. That's... pretty much it.
Do you ever fast for extended periods, push yourself to exercise even when you're tired or not in the mood, or do anything else to burn extra calories after eating?

Um... no. Not really. 

I just... I work on my feet a lot at the plant, so I'm moving around. But I don't... I don't really do all that other stuff. I just watch my food.
Would you say that your weight or how your body looks is more important to how you feel about yourself than other things in your life?

Um... I guess so. I don't know if it's the most important thing, but... it matters. 

Like I said before, if I walk past a shop window or look in the bathroom mirror and my stomach or my thighs look big... it just takes over. I can't stop thinking about it. It just... ruins the whole day. So, yeah... it affects me a lot.
Do you feel that your body weight or shape has been influencing how you judge yourself, more than it should?

Um... I feel like I just answered this. But... yeah, probably. 

Like I said, if I catch my reflection in a shop window or the bathroom mirror... and my stomach or my thighs look too big... that's all I can focus on. It just ruins how I feel for the rest of the day. So... yeah, I guess it does.
